Subject: Dedicated capacity perf validation and SLOs

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so everyone has the same context and next steps:

Key SLOs you shared:
- 95th pct latency target: <= 150 ms for single-stream text-gen (prompt size ~512 tokens)
- 99th pct latency target: <= 300 ms for chat/streaming scenarios
- Throughput target: sustained 2000 tokens/sec per customer peak across region (US)
- Concurrency: expect up to 60 concurrent sessions during holiday peak; many streams are real-time (server->client streaming enabled)

Current environment & constraints:
- Production workload sample (attached acme_production_profile.csv) — mostly short prompts with occasional long completions (~1-2% > 1024 tokens)
- Prefer dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) with VPC connectivity and strict data controls

Immediate next steps (owners):
1) Redwood to provide a proposed dedicated sizing & GPU comparison for SLO targets (Aditya) — due EOD 12/2.
2) Customer to confirm a 2-week POC window and preferred start dates (Sarah/Tom).
3) Exchange of SLO acceptance criteria / success metrics doc (I attached a template: slo_requirements.pdf).

Aditya: please see the workload CSV and highlight any tail concerns and recommended GPU types/bandwidth to meet the 95/99 targets with streaming enabled.

Sarah / Tom — does the above capture everything? Any clarifications on burst vs sustained throughput?

Thanks,
Rafael

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity perf validation and SLOs — sizing notes

Hi all —

I dug into the CSV and the tail behavior. High level recommendation to meet the stated SLOs with streaming enabled:

Summary recommendations:
- GPU families compared: NVIDIA A100 40GB, NVIDIA A100 80GB, NVIDIA H100 80GB.
- For your workload (mostly short prompts, occasional long runs) -- H100s give best single-stream latency and lower 95/99 tails due to improved tensor core perf and fp8 kernels. A100 80GB is close but will need slightly larger cluster to match tails.

Sizing (initial reserved pool):
- Option A (lower cost): 6 x A100-80GB — expected sustained throughput ~2.5k tokens/sec, 95th latency ~180ms (single-stream), 99th ~320ms. Requires tighter batching and prefix cache tuning.
- Option B (recommended for SLO headroom): 4 x H100-80GB — expected sustained throughput ~3.5k tokens/sec, 95th latency ~120-140ms, 99th < 250ms, better headroom for spikes and streaming sessions.

Concurrency & streaming notes:
- Concurrency target 60 sessions: with Option B (4 H100s) we expect comfortable headroom if we reserve per-customer throughput of ~3k tokens/sec with adaptive batching.
- For server->client streaming: we enable chunked responses (streaming) by default; the runtime keeps KV cache hot and flushes in small token chunks. Observed tail impact is minimal on H100s (increase of ~10-20ms on 99th) but can be larger on A100 under high concurrency unless we tune compaction/batching thresholds.

Reserved throughput / runbook:
- Recommend reserving 3k tokens/sec for the account initially (this covers the 2k sustained with 50% buffer). We can configure burst policies to allow 5k tokens/sec for short windows (2-5 minutes) with automatic fallback to hosted variants if capacity exhausted.

POC plan:
- Suggest 2-week POC on 4 x H100 with synthetic load based on your CSV (we can supply a harness) — goals: validate 95/99 latency, streaming tail, and autoscale behavior.
- Deliverables: perf report (95/99/avg), per-route traces, cost estimate for Dedicated pool.

I'll attach a short perf matrix and a sample runbook after I finish the microbenchmarks this afternoon.

—Aditya
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachment: perf_matrix_h100_vs_a100.csv (CSV, 12KB)
